newsitem.title: USA: Simpson struck ex-wife - witnesses tell civil trial.
newsitem.headline: Simpson struck ex-wife - witnesses tell civil trial.

text.p: Two witnesses testified on Tuesday that they saw O.J. Simpson slap his ex-wife, contradicting the former football star's testimony that he never hit her.

Simpson was acquitted in criminal court last year of murdering Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman, but is now fighting civil charges brought by the victims' families and could be forced to pay millions of dollars in damages if he loses the case.
India Rose Allen, a former model, testified on Tuesday that she had seen Simpson slap Nicole Brown Simpson at a Beverly Hills veterinarian's office where Allen worked in 1983.
She said Nicole Brown Simpson came to collect her dogs wearing a gold Spandex exercise outfit with a full-length fur coat over the top.
Simpson drove up as she was leaving and "he was mad, gritting his teeth and with his fists clenched."
Allen said Simpson confronted his wife and said: 'I didn't buy this coat for you to go fuck someone else. I want the coat back.'

"He tried to pull it off her, she jerked away from him and he struck her across the face. Her sunglasses and headband went flying and she had a fading bruise under her eye," the former Playboy playmate said.

Allen said she was shocked by the incident "because they were famous, beautiful people about to have a knock-down, drag-out in front of me." She said the blow was "open-handed on the cheek" and that afterwards the couple each left, saying they would "talk about this at home."
In later testimony, Albert Aguilera, who once lived in Laguna Beach where the Simpsons had rented a beach house, recalled an incident around July 4th 1986, in which he saw Simpson hit his ex-wife.
He said he was walking with a friend in the surf and saw Simpson and Nicole Brown Simpson about 50-60 yards (meters) ahead on the beach.
"It appeared she was teasing him. She was standing in front of him with her back to the sea, he was facing the water.

"Suddenly he slapped her and she fell down. He swung his right hand and she went down," said Aguilera, who said he was at the University of Southern California the same time Simpson was a star running back there.
He said Simpson then crouched over his ex-wife and "became agitated." She said 'no, no' in a crying voice. She was on her knees in the sand," Aguilera said.
He told the court he could not hear any further conversation and that later the woman got up and walked off and eventually Simpson followed her.
As the civil trial resumed after a long six-day holiday weekend, plaintiffs' attorneys meanwhile indicated Simpson's long-time friend and lawyer Robert Kardashian would not testify for them.
Kardashian, who cited attorney-client privilege for not testifying at Simpson's criminal trial last year, has since said publicly he has doubts about Simpson's innocence.

Plaintiffs' lawyer John Kelly said Kardashian had said he would testify but at the last moment had declined, unless subpoened. Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki declined a motion to force Kardashian to testify in the civil trial in which Simpson is being sued by the victims' families for wrongful death.
In another development Tuesday, Judge Fujisaki instructed the jury to disregard testimony Simpson gave last week regarding a lie-detector test he took after the murders of his ex-wife and a friend.
Earlier in the day, Judge Fujisaki instructed the jury to disregard the lie detector test testimony from Simpson.
He said plaintiffs' lawyer Daniel Petrocelli had asked Simpson whether he had failed a polygraph test and that he has scored a minus 22, which Petrocelli said indicated "extreme deception."
Citing attorney-client privilege, Fujisaki also said questions by a lawyer did not constitute evidence.
"You must totally disregard the questions about taking lie detector tests, test scores and their meanings and treat the subject as if you had never heard of it," the judge said.
Simpson's defence lawyer Robert Baker had earlier said he would file a motion for a mistrial if such instructions were not given to the jurors.
